mappings.note: Frequency of a trait in an asexual line records how many generations it has been accumulating, so trait B at 60% arose earlier. Not C 4.4-LO-1: there is no cross and no Mendelian ratio to predict.
Asks what variation buys a species over generations, which is the second clause of LO-1. Not C 3.3, which covers where variation comes from rather than what it leads to.
The demand is dominant-or-recessive, i.e. the F1/F2 evidence that one factor masks the other. Not LO-1: no ratio has to be predicted, only the dominance relation named.
Inherited independently is the dihybrid cross and independent assortment, which LO-1 names. Not LO-2: dominance is assumed here, not the thing being established.
Asks whether the given A x O cross is sufficient to decide which allele is dominant; that inference is exactly LO-2. Not LO-1: no ratio is requested.
Plain statement of human sex determination, the only outcome in this frame that names it.
Ways individuals with a trait increase in a population means selection, drift and gene flow acting on accumulated variation. Not C 4.5: nothing here is evidence of past evolution.
Turns on genes carried on chromosomes in germ cells versus a change confined to body cells, which is LO-2 mechanism. Not C 4.5-LO-1: no population-level accumulation is involved.
Small tiger numbers mean lost variation and drift, a population-genetics consequence. Not C 3.3: the worry is about the population, not about how DNA varies.
Speciation factors (drift, selection, isolation, gene flow) are how variation accumulates into a new species. Not C 4.5, which I reserve for evidence of past evolution.
Tests whether geographical isolation can accumulate divergence in a self-pollinating plant; a speciation-mechanism question, not an evidence one.
Same mechanism question for an asexual organism, where variation arises only by DNA-copying error. Mechanism, so LO-1 rather than C 4.5.

Asks for a characteristic used to judge evolutionary closeness, i.e. evidence. No learning outcome covers evidence (LO-1 is about variation accumulating), so the competency is the most specific true code.
Homology versus analogy is evidence of common ancestry, which no learning outcome in this frame reaches; sits at the competency.
Fossils as evidence of evolution. C 4.5-LO-1 would be false: nothing about variation accumulating is asked.
Interbreeding and common ancestry across human populations is an evidence argument, not a variation-accumulation one.
Better body design probes the misreading of evolution as progress, an interpretive point about evidence rather than about accumulating variation.
Two-character cross so LO-1, but the answer TtWW is reached by inferring the parental GENOTYPE from progeny phenotypes, which is LO-2. Neither code alone answers the item.
Identifying a homologous pair is evidence of common ancestry; no outcome in this frame covers homology.
Closest evolutionary relative: evidence and classification, not variation accumulation.
Asks whether a parent-offspring correlation can establish dominance; a dominance-inference question, not a ratio prediction.
The evolution-classification link is about reading evidence of descent; no learning outcome reaches it.
Definition plus examples of analogous and homologous organs: evidence category.

The verb is outline a project, i.e. design an investigation, which is C 8.2; not C 8.2-LO-3 because no Punnett square is drawn and no predicted ratio is checked. LO-2 is the second code because the thing investigated is which coat colour is dominant.
Fossils for deciding evolutionary relationships: evidence.
Origin of life from inanimate matter (Miller and Urey) is an evidence question about where evolution starts.
Compares how much variation sexual and asexual reproduction generate and ties it to evolution, which is LO-1 almost word for word.
Equal contribution follows from each parent giving one chromosome of every pair: genes carried on chromosomes, LO-2.
Asks whether only advantageous variants survive, i.e. selection versus drift acting on accumulated variation.
Fossils are written documents of ...: fossil evidence, which no learning outcome covers.
Feathers appearing first in dinosaurs is a fossil-evidence fact, not a statement about variation accumulating.
Edible parts of the wild-cabbage derivatives is the artificial-selection illustration, used in the chapter as an analogy for evidence of descent with modification.
Temperature-dependent sex determination is deliberately NOT C 3.3-LO-3, which is restricted to human beings. It sits at the competency as a heredity mechanism that is expressly not chromosomal.
Naming a common human recessive trait (attached ear lobes) is a dominant/recessive classification, LO-2, not a ratio prediction.
Variation good for the species but not for the individual is the population-level consequence of accumulated variation.
Human sex determination, stated directly.
Whether the mother contributes to the sex outcome is answered by XX versus XY: human sex determination.
Features of fossils that help the study of evolution: evidence.
Every female gamete carries X because the mother is XX, which is the mechanism LO-3 describes.
The 50:50 expectation comes from equal numbers of X- and Y-bearing sperm; human sex determination.
Small populations lose variation and drift toward extinction: a population-genetics consequence, not a cross.
Homologous structures and whether they must imply a common ancestor: evidence of evolution.
Whether diversity implies diverse ancestry is an argument from evidence for common descent.
Contrasting pea characters with the dominant member named: dominance classification, not ratio prediction.

Why Mendel chose pea is a question about experimental design: pure lines, clear contrasting characters, controlled pollination. Not C 4.4, since no law, cross or ratio is applied; not C 8.2-LO-3, since no Punnett square is involved.
A woman with only daughters is explained by chance in X- versus Y-bearing sperm: human sex determination.
Whether geographical isolation produces a new species is a speciation-mechanism question.
A simpler body plan does not mean less evolved: the evolution-is-not-progress interpretive point about evidence.
Evidence that all human races share a common ancestor.
Inherited versus acquired rests on whether the change is in the genes carried on the chromosomes of germ cells.
Same germ-line reasoning as 86464, asked as give reasons.
Molecular structures being more conserved than morphological ones is molecular evidence for evolution.

Write the characteristics of the progeny for given crosses is predicting outcomes from Mendel laws. The crosses themselves sat in a figure that did not survive extraction; the skill demanded is still unambiguous.
Self-pollination of F1 and the resulting progeny is a monohybrid cross worked through to F2.
Asks for the F2 combinations and their ratios, which is LO-1 predicts the ratios obtained.
Basic features of the mechanism of inheritance means genes on chromosomes with one set from each parent.
New combinations in F2 are produced by independent assortment, applied in the dihybrid cross.
Struggle for existence and survival of the fittest is natural selection acting on variation.

DEFECTIVE ITEM: a value-based preamble about individual talents is spliced onto an unrelated question about the social impact of emigration and acclimatisation. No competency in this frame is honestly true; emigration and acclimatisation are organism-and-environment, so the goal is the highest honest statement.
Carriers and hereditary disease turn on a recessive factor staying hidden while a dominant one is present, which is LO-2 and not a ratio question.
The wife cannot determine the sex because every egg carries X: human sex determination.

Lamarck is asked for in the context of the acquired-versus-inherited distinction, which LO-2 explains through germ-cell genes. Not C 4.5: the item belongs to the heredity material, not to evidence of evolution.
Vestigial organs are evidence of descent with modification; no learning outcome covers them.
Darwin and natural selection: the mechanism that filters variation over generations, not an evidence question.
Significance of homology between the human hand and a bird wing: evidence of common ancestry.
Naming Mendel as founder of the laws of inheritance uses neither a cross nor a dominance call, so neither LO-1 nor LO-2 is honestly reached; it sits at the competency that names Mendel laws.
Defining inheritance as transmission of traits through genes is LO-2.
Function of genes (one gene, one protein, one characteristic) is the LO-2 mechanism.
What is a gene: a segment of DNA on a chromosome that controls a trait.
Defining speciation names the evolutionary process that accumulated variation produces. Not C 4.5: nothing evidential is asked.
Two factors leading to speciation: mechanism, not evidence.
Definition of homologous organs: the evidence category, which no learning outcome reaches.
Two terms are wanted: genetics, the mechanism by which variation is created and inherited (C 3.3), and evolution, new organisms from existing ones (C 4.5-LO-1). Neither code covers the other half.
Darwin contribution is natural selection, the mechanism, not the fossil or homology evidence.

Why no two individuals are alike is answered by DNA-copying errors and reshuffling, i.e. variation as change in DNA sequence. Not C 4.5-LO-1: the item asks where variation comes from, not what accumulates from it.
Genes are located on chromosomes, which is LO-2 verbatim.
A bare definition of heredity does not invoke genes carried on chromosomes, so it sits at the competency rather than at LO-2.

MISFILED: trophic levels in a food chain belong to the ecosystem chapter, not Heredity. No competency in this frame is true; interconnectedness between organisms and their environment is the only honest statement.
What F1 stands for is Mendelian vocabulary with no cross to apply and no dominance to call, so it sits at the competency and not at either learning outcome.
MISFILED: the feature that distinguishes a bacterial cell (no nuclear membrane) is cell-biology content. Only the goal about the living world at the cellular level is honestly true.
Which of round-yellow or green-wrinkled is the dominant set is a dominance call, not a ratio prediction.
Fossils and what they tell us about evolution: evidence. Verbatim duplicate of qid 86428.
Four ways a trait increases in a population means selection, drift, gene flow and mutation acting over generations.
Justifying or refuting that only advantageous variants survive is selection versus drift on accumulated variation.
The father chromosome decides the sex: human sex determination.
Inherited versus acquired characters with examples: the germ-line gene argument.
Part (a) is the full form of DNA, the molecule named in the competency; part (b) is why variations are essential for the species, which is C 4.5-LO-1. Two halves, two outcomes.
How sexual and asexual reproduction each lead to speciation: mechanism, not evidence.
Four tools for studying evolutionary relationships (fossils, homology, DNA, embryology) are all evidence.
The chromosomal difference between sperm and egg is the whole basis of human sex determination.
Eyes in insects, octopus, planaria and vertebrates are analogous, so the animals cannot be grouped by them: evidence reasoning.
Beetles in a low-food area show a non-genetic weight drop alongside a real population change: variation and its fate over generations.
Making an exact copy is DNA replication, the molecular basis named in the competency. Not LO-2, which is about traits being inherited rather than about copying itself.
Genetic determination of sex at conception in human beings.
Acquired versus inherited traits plus why acquired ones are not passed on: germ-cell genes.
Mendel tall/short experiment traced through F1 and F2 is a monohybrid cross with its ratio.
Homologous structures and how they establish evolutionary relationship: evidence.
Natural selection explained with an example: the mechanism acting on variation.

PP x pp, F1 colour, percentage white in F2 and the PP:Pp ratio are all ratio predictions from a monohybrid cross. Not C 8.2-LO-3: a flow chart is asked for, and no observed count is checked against a prediction.
Fossils plus the analogous-or-homologous call: both halves are evidence of evolution.
Part (a) is the law of dominance read off a monohybrid cross, which is LO-2; part (b) is genetic drift, which is C 4.5-LO-1. Neither code covers the other.
Part (a) speciation factors and part (b) analogous-organ evidence straddle the outcome boundary, so the shared competency is cited rather than LO-1 together with its own parent.
Part (a) intelligence and knowledge are not in the germ-line genes (LO-2); part (b) birds evolved from reptiles rests on fossil and homology evidence (C 4.5).
Organs adapted to new functions, and older body designs not being inefficient, are both interpretations of evolutionary evidence.
Tall versus short explained by the role of genes in controlling characteristics is the gene-to-trait mechanism, not a cross to be worked.
Sorting insect wing, bat wing, frog and human forelimbs into analogous and homologous: evidence.
A dihybrid cross whose F2 is given as OBSERVED counts 314:110:102:32; the work is to predict 9:3:3:1 and check the observation against it, which is precisely the second clause of C 8.2-LO-3.
Three parts (ordering selection, migration, gene flow and new species; analogous wings; artificial versus natural selection) span mechanism and evidence, so the shared competency is the honest code.
Artificial selection in cauliflower, the steps of speciation and human races as one species again span mechanism and evidence; cited at the competency.
Analogous and homologous organs, and how homology explains evolution: evidence throughout.
Traits are inherited independently is the dihybrid cross and independent assortment.
Natural selection and genetic drift in speciation: the mechanism by which variation is fixed in a population.
Part (a) speciation and its factors is C 4.5-LO-1; parts (b) and (c) ask which of eye colour, height, weight-lifting and reading French are genetically inherited, which is C 3.3-LO-2.
Speciation factors plus naming the organs shown and their evidential value: straddles mechanism and evidence, so cited at the competency. The figure did not survive extraction.
Tall-purple crossed with dwarf-white, through F1 to an F2 phenotypic ratio: a dihybrid cross whose ratio must be predicted.
Part (a) the surgically tailless mouse is the germ-line argument (LO-2); part (b) pairing homologous and analogous organs is evidence (C 4.5).
Recent fossils lying nearer the surface (evidence) plus two speciation factors (mechanism); cited at the shared competency.
Naming the human sex chromosomes and tracing an X-bearing sperm to a daughter is human sex determination from end to end.
75 black to 25 white is the 3:1 monohybrid ratio (LO-1), and the item separately demands the parental genotype and which trait is dominant (LO-2). Both codes are load-bearing.
